opportunities.title: Patch Now or Get Popped: F5 BIG-IP, Check Point, and Arista Zero-Days All Under Active Exploit This Week
opportunities.why_now: Three unrelated vendors disclosed actively-exploited zero-days within 48 hours, giving readers a single urgent patch-cadence roundup.
opportunities.angle: Rapid-fire digest format: CVE, vendor, exploitation status, patch deadline for each; end with a 'if you only patch one thing today' verdict.

opportunities.title: ShinyHunters Says They Hacked the FBI — And They Want an Apology, Not Money
opportunities.why_now: The claim, denial-of-motive angle, and demand for a threat-report retraction are unfolding across multiple outlets right now, making it a hot breaking-breach story.
opportunities.angle: Timeline/explainer piece tracking the claim, what data is allegedly stolen (agents, job applicants), and why the group insists it's not financial — with a running-tally update box.

opportunities.title: Meet CLOSEDQUORUM: The Malware That Lets an AI Model Decide What to Do After It Breaks In
opportunities.why_now: This is a genuinely novel threat-actor capability — AI picking post-compromise actions autonomously — that fits the site's inevitable-breach beat with a fresh AI-security twist.
opportunities.angle: Threat-actor profile/explainer: how it works, why it's a step-change from scripted post-exploitation kits, and what defenders should watch for.

opportunities.title: Cl0p Gets Ransomed by ShinyHunters — Now Its Victims Are Exposed Twice
opportunities.why_now: A ransomware gang getting hijacked by a rival is rare, dramatic, and directly threatens Cl0p's existing victim list, a real breach-cascade story.
opportunities.angle: Threat-actor drama piece framed as 'crime doesn't pay (the criminals)' with a sidebar on what Cl0p victims should do now that their data may leak twice.

opportunities.title: A Security Firm Got Hit by the Supply Chain It Warns Everyone About: Shai-Hulud Nips CrowdSec's GitHub
opportunities.why_now: The irony of a threat-intel/cyber-defense company falling to the same npm/GitHub worm it tracks is a perfect inevitable-breach hook.
opportunities.angle: Short, punchy 'even the watchers get watched' post using CrowdSec as a case study for why supply-chain hygiene fails everywhere, including security vendors.
